g.text: NextAurora — EF Core query + write lifecycle (with concurrency tokens)
READ: LINQ → expression tree → provider-specific SQL → DataReader → DTO (no tracker, no entity allocation).

WRITE: load tracked → mutate via domain method → SaveChanges → UPDATE ... WHERE Id=@p AND xmin/RowVersion=@orig (concurrency check). 0 rows matched → DbUpdateConcurrencyException → 409 (HTTP) or Wolverine retry (events).
.Select(p => new ProductDto { Id = p.Id, Name = p.Name, Price = p.Price, ...
Builds Expression<Func<…>> tree · AsNoTracking sets QueryTrackingBehavior on the
Postgres (Npgsql): SELECT p."Id", p."Name", p."Price", ... FROM "Products" p WHERE p."Id" = @__id_0
SQL Server (SqlClient): SELECT TOP(1) [p].[Id], [p].[Name], [p].[Price], ... FROM [Products] AS [p] WHERE
DbConnection.ExecuteReader → DataReader streams rows from the pooled connection
NO Product entity is constructed. NO identity-map entry. NO change-tracking snapshot.
Why this matters: at high RPS, the saved allocations are measurable in GC pressure.
WRITE PATH ▸ load tracked → mutate → SaveChanges → concurrency check
var product = await ctx.Products.FirstAsync(p => p.Id == id); // tracked
// change tracker stores: { Id, Name, Price, ..., xmin = 12345 (or RowVersion = 0x00000000000007D1) }
product.UpdateDetails(name, description, price); // mutate via domain method
// EF emits UPDATE with concurrency-token check in WHERE
Concurrency tokens — different mechanisms per provider
▸ System column on every row; engine auto-increments on every write
▸ NO schema change required — just bind to it as a shadow property:
▸ Old API UseXminAsConcurrencyToken() removed in Npgsql 9+ — manual form is canonical
▸ Real rowversion column the engine maintains on insert/update
▸ REQUIRES a migration to add the column
